FORMAL CASE NO. GA2015-09, IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF T.E.S. 
ENERGY SERVICES, L.P. TO SURRENDER ITS NATURAL GAS SUPPLIER LICENSE 
IN THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA, Order No. 22888 

I. 
INTRODUCTION 
1. 
By this Order,1 the Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia 
(“Commission”) grants the request of T.E.S. Energy Services, L.P. (“TES” or “Applicant”) to 
surrender its natural gas supplier license. Cancellation of the Applicant’s natural gas supplier 
license shall become effective on July 31, 2026. 

II. 
BACKGROUND 
2. 
On September 9, 2016, the Commission granted TES a license to operate as a 
natural gas supplier in the District of Columbia (“District”) in Order No. 18522.2 On May 19, 
2026, TES filed an Application with the Commission to surrender its natural gas supplier license.3 
TES was approved to operate as a broker of natural gas services, but it conducts no business with 
any natural gas customers in the District and no longer requires its supplier license.4 Consequently, 
TES requests to surrender its natural gas supplier license.5 

1

authority to act and issue orders on the following matters: . . . m. Applications for the Abandonment of Gas or Electric 
Licenses”). Any party may file a petition for reconsideration of the General Counsel’s decision with the Commission.

III. 
DISCUSSION 

3. 
According to 15 DCMR § 4702.10 (a)(1), a licensed natural gas supplier wishing 
to cease providing services in the District is required to provide written notice to the Commission 
of the licensee’s intention to cease providing natural gas service to its customers and inform its 
customers of the choice to revert to the default service provider or another natural gas supplier. 
Section 4702.10 (a)(2) also requires that the surrendering licensee provide to the Commission an 
example or copy of the notice provided to its customers and, upon the Commission’s receipt of 
such notice, may order the licensee to provide such further notice to its customers or the public as 
the Commission deems necessary, and/or take such other action that the Commission considers 
appropriate.6 

4. 
In the instant case, TES’s Application provides the required notice to the 
Commission of its intention to surrender its natural gas supplier license, effective July 31, 2026.7 
TES also states that because it provides no service to customers in the District, the notice 
requirement is inapplicable.8 Accordingly, TES’s Application satisfies the notice requirement with 
regard to the cessation of service. 

5. 
In all other respects, TES’s Application conforms with Commission requirements 
for a surrendering licensee. The Applicant has provided the case number, order number, and the 
date the Applicant’s license was granted.9 TES avers, and Commission records confirm, that the 
Applicant’s most recent survey response indicates no jurisdictional revenue and that it owes no 
outstanding debt or fees.10 In addition, the Applicant attests that it has no outstanding consumer 
complaints.11 Lastly, the Applicant has submitted an affidavit from an officer of TES attesting to 
the truth and accuracy of the information submitted.12 

6. 
Based upon the preceding information, the Commission grants TES’s request to 
surrender its natural gas supplier license granted by Order No. 18522. Cancellation of TES’s 
natural gas supplier license shall become effective upon the requested date of July 31, 2026. 
Should TES seek to re-enter the District’s natural gas market in the future, it shall have to reapply 
for a natural gas supplier license pursuant to Chapter 47 of the Commission’s rules.
